name: Washington
uniformActsAdopted: Uniform Guardianship, Conservatorship, and Other Protective Arrangements Act
Revised Uniform Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act

citations.title: Power of attorney — Termination
citations.quote: terminates upon the incapacity of the principal unless the writing contains the words "This power of attorney shall not be affected by disability of the principal" ... or similar words

citations.title: Agent authority — Health care
citations.quote: The agent shall be authorized to act as the principal's personal representative pursuant to the health insurance portability and accountability act

citations.title: Basis for appointment of guardian for adult
citations.quote: the court may ... Appoint a guardian for an adult if the court finds by clear and convincing evidence ... even with appropriate supportive services, technological assistance, or supported decision making

citations.title: Persons entitled to letters
citations.quote: Administration of an estate ... shall be granted to some one or more of the persons hereinafter mentioned ... (a) The surviving spouse or state registered domestic partner

citations.title: Disposition of personal property, debts by affidavit
citations.quote: less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed one hundred thousand dollars; ... That forty days have elapsed since the death of the decedent

citations.title: Applicability
citations.quote: This chapter applies to: (a) A fiduciary acting under a will or power of attorney executed before, on, or after June 9, 2016

citations.title: Right to control disposition of remains
citations.quote: A person has the right to control the disposition of his or her own remains without the predeath or postdeath consent of another person.

assigned.event: Principal signs a writing containing words showing the authority is to survive disability

ends.event: Principal's incapacity, unless the writing carries durability words

patches.diff: Washington did not take the uniform act's default. Authority terminates on the principal's incapacity unless the instrument says it survives disability, so durability is opted INTO here rather than out of.

localNames: power of attorney without durability words

ends.event: Principal becomes incapacitated; this is the default outcome in Washington

patches.diff: This is the Washington default: a power of attorney without durability words ends on incapacity.

localNames: agent with general authority over health care matters

starts.event: Power of attorney grants general authority over health care matters

patches.diff: A general grant of health-care authority also makes the agent the principal's HIPAA personal representative by statute, without separate wording.

assigned.event: Court appoints on petition, after notice and hearing, on clear and convincing evidence

patches.diff: Washington enacted the uniform guardianship and protective arrangements act as RCW 11.130. The court must find the adult cannot meet essential requirements even with supportive services, technological assistance or supported decision making, so those alternatives are weighed before a guardian is appointed.

assigned.event: Letters granted in statutory order, the surviving spouse or state registered domestic partner first

patches.diff: The priority list names a state registered domestic partner alongside the surviving spouse, and lets that person nominate someone else to be appointed in their place.

starts.event: 40 days after death, where probate assets net of liens do not exceed $100,000

patches.diff: The threshold is $100,000 of probate assets net of liens, excluding the surviving spouse's or domestic partner's community property interest, and the wait is 40 days rather than 30.

starts.event: Fiduciary acts for a user who resides or resided in Washington

patches.diff: Washington enacted RUFADAA as RCW chapter 11.120, applying to instruments executed before or after 9 June 2016.

patches.name: Person controlling disposition of remains
localNames: written document expressing the decedent's wishes
patches.summary: A person controls the disposition of their own remains, and a signed, witnessed written document stating their wishes is by itself sufficient authority to carry them out.

assigned.event: Person signs a written document stating their wishes, in the presence of a witness

transitions.event: Written document signed before a witness (RCW 68.50.160(1))
Death; the document is sufficient legal authorisation

patches.diff: Washington gives the person control of their own remains without anyone else's consent, before or after death. The uniform/model baseline has no equivalent role.
